rule: A ✓ means a published, machine-checked proof shows that all the code computing the operation, as that library runs it on that host, gives the specified result for every input: the cipher and its mode, the hash over every block with its padding, the whole scalar multiplication or exponentiation, and the glue around them, such as clamping, byte conversion, and point encoding. Parsing DER key and signature containers, randomness, and the message hash a signature takes are left out. Proofs of memory safety alone, or of only some of the code, earn no ✓.

gaps.reason: Narrowed by [#352](https://github.com/kixel-ai/rind/pull/352): on the SHA extensions the last block is padded and the digest written in registers, and `digest::Context::finish` takes `&mut self`, so it no longer copies the context. Closed by [#394](https://github.com/kixel-ai/rind/pull/394), after this data, which drops the context's wipe on drop: on GitHub's AMD EPYC 9V45 runner it measured rind at 0.84× main's time at 64 B and 0.86× RustCrypto's. The next refresh drops this entry.

Noise: other work kept 5 CPUs busy during this run, in which PSS signing, the same exponentiation, measured 0.95× graviola's time. Interleaved runs on `nixos` the same morning measured rind's PKCS#1 signing at 436 to 446 µs against graviola's 432 to 542 µs and ring's 459 to 568 µs. The next refresh rechecks it.

These VPSes' virtual CPUs hide ADX, and there rind ran s2n-bignum's verified `_alt` routines, which RustCrypto's AVX2 backend beats. Closed by [#415](https://github.com/kixel-ai/rind/pull/415), after this data, which runs a port of that backend there: its collection measured rind at 1.08× RustCrypto's time on both VPSes. The next refresh drops this entry.
Noise from the VPS's other tenants: `ovh-sea`, the same virtual CPU, measured 0.92× aws-lc-rs's time, and no dedicated host shows it. The next refresh rechecks it.

CPUs older than Broadwell and Zen lack ADX, and so do virtual CPUs that hide it, as `ovh-iad`'s and `ovh-sea`'s do. There rind runs s2n-bignum's verified `_alt` routines, which trail by more than 10% only on GitHub's runners: on the VPSes P-256 verification measured 1.05× aws-lc-rs's time.
Without SSE4.1 rind runs Graviola's scalar Poly1305 rather than port BoringSSL's SSE2 `poly1305_vec.c` for CPUs older than Westmere, as ALGORITHMS.md records.

DIT: the M4 has it, and rind turns it on and off around every call that handles a secret, which costs about 30 to 55 ns a call there; the other libraries never set it. Keeping it per call was decided with the maintainer from [#387](https://github.com/kixel-ai/rind/pull/387)'s findings. Holding `rind::cpu::Dit::hold()` ([#431](https://github.com/kixel-ai/rind/pull/431)) across a batch of calls, as MoQ does, pays it once and closes all but one of these gaps: the rind (DIT held) column times that, and on [`9e7f6a5a`](https://github.com/kixel-ai/rind/commit/9e7f6a5a9ea59a0cf1251c24af6c5d4f21c2b0fd), the run this report shows, every one measured within 10% of the fastest library except HMAC-SHA-256 at 64 B, at 1.10× RustCrypto's (109.7 ns against 99.4 ns).

Closed by [#700](https://github.com/kixel-ai/rind/pull/700), after this data, which keeps the portable backend's verification in fiat-crypto's limbs across the whole twin multiplication, converts between them and words by shifts, and compares x without an inversion: on an otherwise idle Ryzen 9 5900XT under `--cfg rind_portable`, verification measured 0.80 to 0.97× aws-lc's C time, from 1.07 to 1.16× before, and every other P-521 benchmark at most 0.95×. The next refresh drops this entry.

Closed in part by [#614](https://github.com/kixel-ai/rind/pull/614), after this data, which runs RSA and the NIST curves on 64-bit limbs on 64-bit targets. On a shared x86_64 host it measured, against aws-lc-rs's C without assembly: P-256 and P-384 at 0.44 to 0.76× its time, P-521 ECDH, key generation, and signing at 0.91 to 1.03×, the rustls handshakes at 0.64 to 0.96× but those the entry above names, and every ranked JWT benchmark at 0.55 to 1.06×. RSA's rows are closed by [#702](https://github.com/kixel-ai/rind/pull/702), which adds two rows a pass in two carry chains and splits wide products by Karatsuba's method: the median of nine runs on a shared x86_64 host measured PKCS#1 signing and verification at 2048 through 8192 bits at 0.85 to 0.97× aws-lc-rs's time, and three runs the rustls handshakes on RSA-3072 and RSA-4096 keys at 0.63 to 0.99×. The next refresh drops this entry.

Narrowed by [#621](https://github.com/kixel-ai/rind/pull/621), after this data, which runs aws-lc's `aes_nohw.c` in its 64-bit configuration, four blocks a pass, in place of the one-block libcrux cipher: on a shared x86_64 host under `--cfg rind_portable` AES-GCM measured 0.18× its previous time and 0.93 to 1.11× aws-lc's from 1200 B, and 0.5 to 0.9× below that, and CBC encryption 0.55 to 0.67×. AES-CTR and CBC decryption remain 1.08 to 1.23× aws-lc's: this row builds aws-lc's C for x86_64, where it bitslices eight blocks into SSE2 registers, while rind's portable backend runs the configuration aws-lc itself runs on the other 64-bit targets the backend is for. The next refresh rechecks it.

rind's portable SHA-1 and HACL*'s verified SHA-384/512, through libcrux-sha2, trail aws-lc's C by 1.1 to 1.3× from 1200 B up. Kept: verified HACL* within 1.3× is worth more than an unverified source on targets without assembly, which are the cold tiers.
